A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying tracking framework, renamed from UA-Track to S2-Track. Their readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes tracking and detection results, component ablations, uncertainty analyses, qualitative comparisons, and inference-speed measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional comparisons and revised subgroup results, including in its appendices.

M1.justification: UQI becomes PQI and UQD becomes HQD, but their procedures remain 2D/depth-based query initialization and IoU-thresholded denoising. Gaussian attention, auxiliary objectives, and the overall loss also match. The new query-encoding description supplies implementation detail rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate nuScenes 3D tracking and detection, including occlusion, object-size, and distance conditions. Revised subgroup boundaries repartition existing coverage; no additional dataset, domain, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: The comparison suite changes across several experiments. Tracking Table 1 adds MSGLMB, Cyclic, RockTrack, HSTrack, and ADA-Track and removes TripletTrack. Table 2 adds Cyclic and ADA-Track while removing CenterTrack and TripletTrack. Appendix detection comparisons add Cyclic on both splits and HSTrack on validation; core PF-Track and Sparse4D-v3 comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v1 Section 6.2 uses four visibility groups and two size groups separated at 2.5 meters. v2 Appendix A.2.4 merges the upper visibility groups into 60–100% and uses three size groups with cutoffs at 2 and 3.5 meters. The main dataset splits, resolutions, training budgets, and hardware settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The challenge analysis is revised through different visibility and size groupings, and the main qualitative comparison contains fewer frames and scenes. Component, denoising-threshold, feature-stride, decoder, and uncertainty analyses otherwise remain; moving or redrawing them does not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Both Table 3 versions retain the same MC-dropout and ensemble uncertainty estimates, including entropy and standard deviation. Neither adds seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports V2-99 full-resolution validation AMOTA of 0.566; the earlier small-resolution 0.458 remains in Table 3, so this is not a same-setting improvement. Comparator entries and re-binned subgroup results change, and decoder-ablation MOTP entries disappear. Headline validation/test AMOTA remains 0.652/0.663, with shared detection, component-ablation, and latency results largely unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.3 explicitly defines the denoising attention mask with a piecewise equation; v2 omits that mathematical definition while retaining masking in Figure 2. Other mathematical assumptions and loss equations match after renumbering, and neither version provides theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution is redefined from addressing overlooked uncertainty through three uncertainty-oriented modules to systematically improving query initialization, propagation, and matching. v2 treats UPD as the explicitly uncertainty-focused component. The headline 66.3% test AMOTA and 8.9-point advantage remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains denoising through unstable bipartite matching and interprets PQI/HQD uncertainty reductions as benefits outside their primary motivation (Section 3.4 and Appendix B.2). Its Impact Statement replaces uncertainty-focused future work with discussion of camera–LiDAR extension and privacy.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2.3 adds coordinate normalization, sinusoidal encoding, and linear-projection details for query initialization. Conversely, v2 removes the project-site link and v1's statement that UPD/UQD operate only during training. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding procedural changes.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from an uncertainty-centered contribution toward comprehensive improvement of query-based tracking. Much uncertainty background moves into Section 3.3 rather than disappearing. v2 adds recent tracking references and a substantive comparison with 3DPPE in Appendix B.1, while dropping the face-recognition uncertainty reference.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion are extensively reframed. Method sections are reordered, terminology changes throughout, related work is reorganized, experimental setup moves into the appendix, and a new Additional Discussion section appears.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 gains a pipeline overview, the decoder diagram is reoriented, challenge plots become Table 4, and qualitative panels are shortened and compressed. Appendix visualizations are enlarged onto separate pages, and multiple tables change structure and placement.

improvement.justification: Updated baselines and the full-resolution V2-99 validation comparison improve empirical context, while query-encoding details and the 3DPPE discussion improve technical clarity. These gains are limited because the method and headline evidence remain stable. Losing the explicit mask definition and project link, and compressing the main qualitative figures, partly offsets the benefits.
